Count position scale with an optional pseudo-log transform

Source: R/scale.R
seq_scale_count.Rd

Builds a continuous y scale for copy-number style counts with integer tick labels. In log mode values up to 1 stay linear and larger values map to 1 + log2(v), so ticks fall at 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, ... When a track uses this scale, elements added to it transform their mapped y fields (see the y_fields field of SeqElementR6) before mapping to the canvas. Constant aesthetics such as aes(height = ) are not transformed.

Usage

seq_scale_count(
  max,
  log = max > 8,
  bottom = 0.018,
  top_pad = 0.5,
  expand = c(0.025, 0),
  oob = c("exclude", "perimeter")
)

Arguments

max

Largest count to show. Values below 1 are raised to 1.

log

Logical. Use the pseudo-log transform. Default max > 8.

bottom

Fraction of the top value reserved below 0, so that drawings offset beneath 0 stay visible. Default 0.018.

top_pad

Headroom above the top tick in linear mode. Default 0.5.

expand

Length-2 c(mul, add) padding, as in seq_scale_continuous().

oob

Out-of-bounds handling, as in seq_scale_continuous().

Value

A SeqScaleCount / SeqScaleContinuous_Pos / SeqPositionScale object with extra fields transform and inverse (functions, or NULL in linear mode) and log.

Examples

s <- seq_scale_count(12, log = TRUE)
s$labels
#> [1] "0"  "1"  "2"  "4"  "8"  "16"
s$transform(12)
#> [1] 4.584963
seq_scale_count(8)$breaks
#> [1] 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8
